cards.text: Isaiah son of Amoz is a prophet with a message about Judah and Jerusalem (Isaiah 2:1). He's just warned that the Day of the LORD of Hosts is coming against all the proud and lofty (Isaiah 2:12). Now he says behold: the Lord GOD of Hosts is about to remove both supply and support from Jerusalem and Judah.

cards.question: The Lord GOD of Hosts is about to take away Jerusalem's supply. What's on that list?

answers.text: The whole supply of food and water
All the gold in the treasury

cards.question: The Lord is also taking away the support Jerusalem and Judah lean on. What is that support?

cards.text: On the way out: the mighty man, the warrior, the judge, the prophet, the soothsayer, the elder, the commander of fifty, the dignitary, the counselor, the cunning magician and the clever enchanter. Friend, that's not a list, that's the WHOLE org chart.

cards.question: With all those leaders on the way out, the Lord says He will put kings from other nations in charge of Jerusalem and Judah.

cards.text: Not kings from anywhere. The Lord says, "I will make mere lads their leaders, and children will rule over them."

cards.question: With mere lads leading Jerusalem and Judah, how will the people treat each other?

answers.text: They will share what they have
They will stay out of each other's way

cards.text: Man against man, neighbor against neighbor, the young against the old, the base against the honorable. Then a man seizes his own brother inside his father's house to make him leader, and friend, the bar is LOW.

cards.question: The man tells his brother he should be their leader because he has a ___.

cards.text: He says, "You have a cloak—you be our leader! Take charge of this heap of rubble." That's like getting promoted to manager because you're the only one in the office who owns a STAPLER.

cards.question: The brother happily agrees to take charge of the heap of rubble.

cards.text: On that day he cries aloud, "I am not a healer. I have no food or clothing in my house. Do not make me leader of the people!" First time I've ever heard somebody turn down a job by listing everything he DOESN'T have.
Now Isaiah steps back and looks at the big picture. Jerusalem has stumbled and Judah has fallen, and he tells us why.

cards.question: Why have Jerusalem stumbled and Judah fallen?

answers.text: They spoke and acted against the LORD
Their armies were too small to win
Their walls were not strong enough

cards.text: They've been defying His glorious presence. And Isaiah says the expression on their faces testifies against them.

cards.question: Isaiah says the people of Jerusalem and Judah work hard to hide their sin.

cards.text: Like the city of Sodom (Genesis 19), they flaunt their sin and don't conceal it, and Isaiah says, "Woe to them, for they have brought disaster upon themselves." That's me standing next to an empty cookie box with crumbs all over my mustache, not even TRYING to wipe them off.

cards.question: Then Isaiah turns to the righteous. What should they be told?

answers.text: It will be well with them
They will fall with the rest

cards.question: The righteous will enjoy the fruit of their labor. But woe to the wicked, who will be repaid with what their ___ have done.
Now God speaks about the ones guiding His people. He tells His people their guides are keeping them on the right paths.

cards.text: God says youths oppress His people and women rule over them, and then: "O My people, your guides mislead you; they turn you from your paths." That's a GPS that's loud, confident and driving you straight into a lake.
Then the LORD arises to contend. He stands to judge the people, and friend, when the Judge stands up, everybody else gets REAL quiet.

cards.question: The LORD brings a charge. Who is it against?

answers.text: The elders and leaders of His people
The kings of the nations around Judah
The priests who serve in the temple

cards.text: He tells them, "You have devoured the vineyard." Then He names what's sitting in their houses.

cards.question: The LORD tells the elders and leaders that the plunder of the ___ is in their houses.

cards.text: "Why do you crush My people and grind the faces of the poor?" declares the Lord GOD of Hosts. Friend, that is NOT a question you want aimed at you.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 12 quotes "You have devoured the vineyard.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Nothing before this card tells the baker what 'support' means here. Card 1 only says 'supply and support.' 'Its walls and towers' is just as reasonable a pick as 'Its leaders and advisers,' so getting it right comes down to luck. It isn't one of the few allowed discovery questions either, because it's a meaning question the setup could make answerable.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: Card 8 ends with 'friend, the bar is LOW,' right before card 9 asks why the man picks his brother. That line tells the baker the reason is something trivial, which rules out 'sword' and 'field' and leaves 'cloak.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Isaiah 3:6-7 is a prediction ('A man will seize his brother…', 'On that day he will cry aloud'). Cards 8 and 12 tell it in the present tense as if it's happening ('Then a man seizes his own brother', 'On that day he cries aloud'). Card 7 keeps the future ('They will oppress one another'). The docs don't say whether predicted scenes in a prophetic passage can be told in the storyteller's present tense.
findings.question: In prophetic passages, can Papa Dorin tell predicted events in the present tense, as if they're happening, or must he keep the text's future tense ('will')?

findings.problem: 'Then Isaiah turns to the righteous' says the righteous are being spoken to. Isaiah 3:10 says 'Tell the righteous,' which is a message to be passed on to them by someone the text doesn't name. This setup also sits in the question itself, because story card 5 doesn't set up the turn.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Card 8 follows two choice cards about Isaiah 3:10-11, and its question brings in a new moment ('Now God speaks about the ones guiding His people'). That setup was never told on a story card.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is on a story card. Not every choice card needs its own story card right before it: a choice card can follow another choice card when the setup is already told.
